auth.title: Sign in
auth.description: Use the account created with v1per init, or one an administrator made for you.

errorBoundary.title: This page failed to render
errorBoundary.description: The rest of the app still works. Try again, or open another page.

errors.unauthenticated: Your session ended. Sign in again.
errors.not_found: This is not available. It does not exist, or your account has no access.
errors.forbidden: Your role does not allow this.
errors.origin_rejected: The request was blocked because it did not come from this app. Reload the page.
errors.stale_revision: Someone changed this since you opened it. Reload to see the current version, then apply your change again.
errors.idempotency_conflict: This request was already sent with different values. Reload and try again.
errors.malformed_request: The app sent a request the server could not read. Reload the page.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.query_timeout: The server took longer than 30 seconds and stopped. Try again.
errors.internal: Something went wrong on the server. Try again.
errors.network: The server did not answer. Check the connection and try again.
errors.second_factor_required: Enter the code from your authenticator app.
errors.second_factor_invalid: That code is wrong or was already used. Try the next one.
errors.second_factor_enrollment_required: Set up two-factor authentication to continue.
errors.operation_not_granted: This API key may not do that.
errors.grant_exceeds_principal: The key would hold more than your role allows on that node.
errors.node_not_empty: Nodes were added below this one. Check the count and confirm again.

home.title: Home
home.noAccessHint: Your account holds no role on any node. Ask an admin for an invitation.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.description: The address does not match any page.

capabilities.nodeRead: Read the node and its subtree

nodes.noChildrenWritable: No child nodes yet. Add one for a team, a client or a project.
nodes.name: Name

create.title: Add child node

create.tooDeep: The tree is {max} levels deep here, the most it may be.

settings.title: Node settings
settings.name: Name
settings.nameDescription: How the node shows in the tree and on its pages.
settings.needsOwner: Owners of this node do this.
settings.twoFactorDescription: Everyone with a role on this node or below must use a second factor. People without one set it up at their next request.
settings.twoFactorInherited: A node above already requires it, so it applies here either way.
settings.placeDescription: Moving changes who sees the node: access comes from roles on the nodes above.

move.title: Move {name}
move.pickDescription: Pick the new parent. Nodes you cannot use say why.
move.reviewDescription: New place: {target}. Check who gains or loses access before you confirm.
move.belowHint: Roles on this node and below move with it.

refusal.capability: Your role here does not allow adding nodes
refusal.depth: Too deep: the tree allows {max} levels

delete.description: Deletes the node with its roles, invitations and API keys. This cannot be undone.
delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.cascade: {count} node below it goes too. | {count} nodes below it go too.
delete.empty: The node has nothing below it.
delete.warning: Everything below is deleted with it, including roles and API keys there.

nodes.pageCount: {count} page here and below | {count} pages here and below

members.title: Members
members.readOnly: Your role shows who has access. Admins and owners invite people and change roles.
members.inheritHint: A role applies to the node and everything below it. Change an inherited role on the node it comes from.
members.leaveConfirm: Give up your role on {node}? Roles on nodes above stay.
members.removeConfirm: Remove the role of {name} on {node}? Roles on nodes above stay.

refusal.rank: Same or higher role than yours

invitations.title: Invitations
invitations.createDescription: Invite one person to {node}. They get access to everything below it too.
invitations.createdDescription: Send this link to {email}. It works once.
invitations.roleHint: You can invite with roles below your own.

secrets.once: Copy it now. It is shown only this once.
secrets.withheld: This answer was repeated, so the secret is not shown again. Create a new one if you did not keep it.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.description: A code from an authenticator app at every sign-in, on top of your password.
twoFactor.requiredHint: A node you have a role on requires it, so it cannot be turned off.
twoFactor.regenerateConfirm: Your current recovery codes stop working.
twoFactor.regeneratedDescription: The old codes no longer work.
twoFactor.disableConfirm: Sign-in then needs your password only.
twoFactor.codesOnce: Keep these codes somewhere safe. Each works once if you lose your phone. They are shown only now.
twoFactor.codesWithheld: This answer was repeated, so the codes are not shown again. Create new ones if you did not keep them.
twoFactor.codesKept: I have kept the recovery codes
twoFactor.challengeDescription: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.challengeRecovery: Enter one of your recovery codes.
twoFactor.challengeExpired: This sign-in step ended: it lasts {minutes} minutes and {attempts} attempts. Start again with your password.

setup.description: Connect an authenticator app such as 1Password, Bitwarden or Google Authenticator.
setup.step2: Scan the QR code, or type the key.
setup.qr: QR code for your authenticator app
setup.codeHint: The {digits} digits your app shows now.
setup.withheld: This answer was repeated, so the key is not shown again. Go back and start over.

enroll.title: Set up two-factor
enroll.description: A node you have a role on requires a second factor. Set one up for {email} to continue.

reauth.title: Confirm it is you
reauth.description: Enter your password. Sensitive changes then pass without asking for {minutes} minutes.

join.title: Join
join.invalid: This invitation link does not work. It was used, revoked or has expired. Ask for a new one.
join.otherAccount: This invitation is for {email}. Accepting adds the role to {account}.
join.signInFirst: An account for {email} exists. Sign in to accept.
join.name: Your name
join.nameHint: Up to {max} characters, shown to people you work with.

security.title: Security
security.passwordDescription: Changing it signs out your other sessions.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.description: Send a key as {scheme} token. It acts as you on one node and below, with only the capabilities you pick.
apiKeys.name: Name
apiKeys.nameHint: Up to {max} characters, to tell keys apart.
apiKeys.nodeHint: The key reaches {node} and everything below it.
apiKeys.notHeld: Your role on this node does not include it.
apiKeys.revokeConfirm: Requests with {name} stop working at once.
apiKeys.createDescription: Pick the node and what the key may do there.
apiKeys.createdDescription: Send it in the Authorization header as {scheme} token.

instance.title: Instance settings
instance.generalDescription: The name shows in the app and the authenticator app. Invitation links start with the public URL.
instance.name: Name
instance.publicUrlHint: The address people use to reach this instance, for example https://status.example.com.
instance.fixed: Set by {variable} on the server, so it cannot change here.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Times in messages, and maintenance without its own timezone, use this zone.
notifications.timezoneHint: An IANA zone, such as Europe/Vienna.
notifications.expiryDaysHint: Days before a certificate expires, comma-separated, such as 7, 14, 21.

smtp.title: Mail server
smtp.description: Email channels without their own server send through this one.
smtp.none: No mail server is set, so email channels need their own.
smtp.fromHint: The sender of every email that does not set its own.
smtp.removeConfirm: Email channels without their own server stop sending until you set one again.
smtp.testDescription: Sends one message through the server as the form above has it, so you can try it before saving.

imports.title: Imports
imports.description: Uptime Kuma databases brought in with v1per import kuma.
imports.emptyHint: Stop the server and run v1per import kuma --source kuma.db --into <node> to bring in an Uptime Kuma database. Its result shows here.
imports.resumeHint: This import did not finish. Run the same v1per import kuma command again to resume it.

logins.title: Logins
logins.meta: Kuma users and how they sign in now

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.meta: what was not mapped, or mapped with a loss

monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.empty: No monitors on this node yet
monitors.emptyHint: Add one to check a website, a port or a server, or to receive pushes from a job.
monitors.readOnly: Members, admins and owners add and change monitors.

summary.title: Monitors
summary.empty: No monitors on this node yet.

detail.latencyEmpty: No response times in this range.
detail.latencySummary: Average response time, {count} points from {from} to {to}.
detail.paused: Paused. No checks run until you resume it.
detail.deleteConfirm: Delete {name} and all its checks? This cannot be undone.
detail.manualHint: A manual monitor shows the status you set. Without one it is pending.
detail.pushHint: Call this URL from your job. No status or status=up counts as up, anything else as down.
detail.unsupported: Imported from Uptime Kuma as {type}. v1per does not run this type, so it stays paused.
detail.alertsEmpty: No alerts sent for this monitor yet.

typeNotes.http: Up when the URL answers with an accepted status code.
typeNotes.keyword: Up when the response contains the keyword.
typeNotes.json-query: Up when a JSON query on the response matches the expected value.
typeNotes.port: Up when a TCP connection opens.
typeNotes.ping: Up when the host answers ICMP echo.
typeNotes.dns: Up when the lookup returns records.
typeNotes.push: Up while your job calls the push URL in time.
typeNotes.group: Down when a member is down. Pick this group in a member's settings.
typeNotes.manual: Shows the status you set on its page.

editor.name: Name
editor.groupHint: Group monitors on this node or above it.
editor.invertKeyword: Up when the keyword is missing
editor.jsonPathHint: A JSONata expression. Empty compares the whole response.
editor.retryOnlyOnStatusCodeFailure: Down at once when the comparison fails
editor.retryOnlyOnStatusCodeFailureHint: Only failed requests use the retries.
editor.headersHint: Seal a header that carries a key; its value is stored encrypted and never shown again.
editor.retryIntervalHint: While pending. Empty uses the interval.
editor.maxRetriesHint: Failed checks shown as pending before the monitor is down.
editor.resendIntervalHint: Down checks between repeated alerts. 0 sends one.
editor.upsideDownHint: Up when the check fails, down when it passes.
editor.quorumHint: When the monitor is down, counted over the probes that run it.
editor.probesHint: Where the check runs. With none picked, the built-in probe runs it.
editor.pushNew: The push URL shows here after you add the monitor.
editor.pushHidden: Members, admins and owners see the push URL.
editor.newTokenHint: The current URL stops working when you save.
editor.pushTokenLength: A push token has {min} to {max} characters.

secret.sealed: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again.

editor.unsupported: This monitor was imported with a type v1per does not run, so it cannot be edited here.
editor.notificationsHint: Where its down, up and certificate alerts go.
editor.channelsHint: Channels of this node and the nodes above. Until you pick, a new monitor gets the default channels.
editor.noChannels: No channels here yet. Add one under Notifications.
editor.expiryNotificationHint: At the days set in the instance settings, by default 21, 14 and 7 days before.
editor.expiryNotificationIgnored: Has no effect while invalid certificates are accepted.

probes.title: Probes
probes.inheritedHint: These probes can check monitors here too. They are managed on the node they belong to.
probes.createDescription: A probe runs checks from another machine. It only opens outbound connections to this server, so it works behind NAT.
probes.name: Name
probes.nameHint: Where it runs, such as Frankfurt or Office. Up to {max} characters.
probes.createdDescription: Run this on the machine that should run the checks. It shows as online once it connects.
probes.commandHint: Add --data-dir for where it keeps results while the server is unreachable. Set V1PER_PROBE_TOKEN instead of --token to keep the token out of the process list.
probes.skewedHint: Its clock differs from the server's by more than 5 seconds, so its check times are off by as much.
probes.emptyHint: Add a probe to check monitors from another network or region.
probes.emptyReadOnly: No probes are registered on this node.
probes.readOnly: Admins of this node add and revoke probes.
probes.revokeConfirm: Revoke {name}? Its agent is refused at its next request and stops, and its monitors no longer use it. This cannot be undone.

channels.title: Notifications
channels.deleteConfirm: {name} and its delivery log will be deleted.
channels.deleteConfirmUsed: {name} and its delivery log will be deleted. {count} monitor stops alerting through it. | {name} and its delivery log will be deleted. {count} monitors stop alerting through it.
channels.readOnly: Admins of this node manage its channels. You see which channels its monitors can use.
channels.emptyHint: Add an email or Discord channel, then pick it for monitors. Default channels join every new monitor here and below.
channels.emptyReadOnly: Neither this node nor the nodes above it have a channel.
channels.noneOwn: None on this node. Monitors here can use the channels above.
channels.inheritedHint: Monitors on this node can use these too. They are managed on the node they belong to.
channels.inactiveHint: This channel is turned off and queues nothing.

editor.basicsHint: Where alerts go and which monitors use it.
editor.providerHint: Imported channels of other Kuma providers are kept but cannot send.
editor.name: Name
editor.isDefaultHint: New monitors on this node and below use it unless their creator picks channels.
editor.applyExistingHint: Links every monitor on this node and below to this channel when you save.
editor.unsupported: This channel was imported from Uptime Kuma and cannot send from v1per: {reason} You can delete it.

smtp.ownServerHint: This channel sends through the server below.
smtp.instanceServerHint: Sends through the instance mail server in the instance settings.
smtp.securityHint: STARTTLS usually runs on port 587 or 25, TLS on port 465.
smtp.ignoreStarttlsHint: Sends in plain text even when the server offers STARTTLS.
smtp.recipientsHint: Comma-separated addresses. Fill in at least one of To, CC and BCC.
smtp.subject: Subject template
smtp.subjectHint: Empty uses Kuma's subject, such as "[API] [🔴 Down] timeout".
smtp.bodyHint: Empty uses Kuma's message with the time in the instance timezone.
smtp.htmlBodyHint: Only applies to a custom body.
smtp.headersHint: A JSON object, sealed like a password.

formatHints.normal: An embed with the service, its address, the time and the error.
formatHints.minimalist: One line, such as "🔴 API is down."
formatHints.custom: Your template, rendered with Kuma's variables.

discord.prefixMessageHint: Text above the embed, for example a role mention.
discord.suppressNotificationsHint: Members see the message without a push notification.

templates.title: Template variables
templates.intro: Templates use Liquid, as in Uptime Kuma, so imported templates send the same text.
templates.noMonitor: Test and certificate messages have no monitor, so they show the test values.

variables.name: The monitor's name
variables.msg: Kuma's message line, such as "[API] [🔴 Down] timeout"
variables.heartbeatJSON: The check: status, time, ping, message, timezone

test.title: Test
test.hint: Sends one message with the form as it is, stored secrets included.
test.storedHint: Sends one message with the saved settings.
test.failed: The test message was not delivered.
test.invalid: Fill in the required fields first.

incidents.dismissConfirm: "{title}" and its timeline will be deleted, as for a false alarm.
incidents.readOnly: Members of this node manage its incidents. You can read them.
incidents.emptyHint: A failing monitor opens one by itself. You can open one for anything else.

auto.openedBy: Opened when this monitor went down:

auto.edited: Someone changed it, so a person resolves it.

targets.none: No monitors or static components on this node or below.

editor.title: Title
editor.titleHint: What people notice, such as "Checkout is slow".
editor.affectedHint: Pick the monitors and static components it affects, each with its impact.
editor.affectedEditHint: A target you take out loses its impact. One you add has none until an update names it.

update.title: Post an update
update.messageHint: What is known and what happens next.
update.resolvedHint: Resolving sets every affected target to operational.

pages.title: Status pages
pages.none: No status page shows what this incident affects.
pages.publishAll: Publish to {count} page | Publish to {count} pages

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.deleteConfirm: "{title}" will be deleted. Its monitors are checked and alert again when it was active.
maintenance.readOnly: Members of this node plan its maintenance. You can read it.
maintenance.emptyHint: Plan a window and its monitors report maintenance instead of alerting.
maintenance.emptyReadOnly: Nothing is planned for this node.

strategyHints.manual: Active from when you save it until you pause it.
strategyHints.recurring-interval: A daily window that repeats every given number of days.
strategyHints.recurring-weekday: A window on the weekdays you pick.
strategyHints.recurring-day-of-month: A window on the days of the month you pick.
strategyHints.cron: Windows that start on a cron schedule and last a set time.

editor.title: Title
editor.lastDayOfMonth: The last day of every month too
editor.cronHint: Five fields, such as "30 3 * * 0" for Sundays at 03:30. Six fields start with seconds.
editor.endTimeHint: An end before the start runs past midnight.
editor.rangeHint: Optional. Leave both empty to repeat for good.
editor.timezoneHint: Times above are in this zone. Empty uses the instance timezone.
editor.monitorsHint: They report maintenance and send no alerts while a window is active. Members of a covered group are covered too.
editor.noMonitors: No monitors on this node or below yet.

preview.incomplete: Fill in the schedule to see its windows.
preview.none: This schedule has no upcoming window.

components.intro: Status page entries without a monitor, such as "Support" or "Billing". Incidents can name them, and status pages show them.
components.dialogDescription: Its color on status pages comes from incidents and maintenance only.
components.name: Name
components.deleteConfirm: {name} will be deleted, and incidents stop naming it.
components.emptyHint: Add one for a service you cannot check with a monitor.
components.emptyReadOnly: Admins of this node add components.

pages.title: Status pages
pages.intro: Pages that show the status of monitors and components on this node and below, for the public, clients or your team. New pages are for your team until you open them up.
pages.createDescription: You pick its components and who can open it next.
pages.emptyHint: Create one to show your services' status to others.
pages.emptyReadOnly: Admins of this node create status pages.
pages.unavailable: This status page is not available.
pages.readOnly: Only admins of this node change status pages. You can preview it.

settings.title: Title
settings.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. The page opens at {path}.
settings.lookHint: Visitors see the page in these colors. Auto follows their device.
settings.logoHint: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG, up to {max} KB.
settings.logoTooLarge: This file is larger than {max} KB.
settings.logoInvalid: This file is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG image.
settings.languagesHint: Visitors get their browser's language when the page offers it, else the default.
settings.timezoneHint: Each bar covers one day in this timezone.
settings.autoIncidentsHint: Incidents opened when a monitor on this page goes down.

autoModeHints.draft: They stay internal until someone publishes them to this page.
autoModeHints.auto_publish: They show on this page once they stayed open for the grace period.

settings.graceHint: 0 to {max}. An outage that ends sooner never shows.
settings.deleteHint: Its address, domains and share links stop working. Incidents stay.
settings.deleteConfirm: {title} will be deleted with its layout, domains and share links.

layout.intro: Pick monitors and components from this node and below, sort them into groups, and save. Drag a row by its handle or use the arrows.
layout.addDescription: Each monitor or component shows once on a page.
layout.nothingToAdd: Everything on this node and below is on the page already.
layout.emptyHint: Add monitors or components to show their status on the page.
layout.count: {count} component on the page | {count} components on the page
layout.outdated: Someone changed this page since you started. Saving will be refused until you load the current version, which drops your changes.

access.grantLogin: People with a role on this node or above always get in by signing in. They see the team view with response times and team-only components. This does not work on custom domains.
access.public: Anyone with the address can open the page
access.publicHint: Off: only the team and the ways below get in.
access.whenRestricted: Applies while the page is not public.
access.passwordHint: Visitors who know it get in for 30 days.
access.passwordRemoved: The password is removed when you save.
access.emailHint: Listed people request a link by email that opens the page.
access.noSmtp: Sign-in links need SMTP. An instance admin sets it up in the instance settings.
access.domainsHint: Anyone with an address at these domains, one per line.

tokens.title: Share links
tokens.intro: A share link opens the page without signing in, until it expires or you revoke it.
tokens.introPublic: The page is public, so share links are not needed now. They work again once it is restricted.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.nameHint: Who it is for, up to {max} characters.
tokens.revokeConfirm: {name} stops working at once, also for visitors who opened the page with it.

hostnames.stepProxy: Add the domain to the proxy so it requests a certificate and passes the Host header on unchanged.
hostnames.grantNote: Signing in as a team member works only at this instance's own address, not on custom domains.
hostnames.runbook: The runbook has examples for Caddy and nginx under "Reverse proxy and custom domains".

preview.publicHint: What the public, password, sign-in link and share link visitors see.
preview.internalHint: What your team sees after signing in, with team-only components and response times.
